question: Can the three NCR freshwater-related rows in the DENR-BMB 2019 inland-wetlands inventory be linked to PSA city codes while preserving source names and unresolved feature identity?
method: Reviewed the NCR freshwater-related rows on page 3 of the official DENR-BMB 2019 inland-wetlands PDF and matched the printed city labels against the PSA NCR city table. Kept the BMB waterbody labels and wetland types verbatim. La Mesa Reservoir matches an existing source-named historical study locality; Jamboree Lake and the Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife Center pond row remain source-row candidates without canonical feature crosswalks. Recorded administrative codes only; did not infer feature boundaries, local access, fish presence, or current water conditions.
sourceRows: Jamboree Lake | NCR | Muntinlupa City | Lake | 2.64 ha
La Mesa Reservoir | NCR | Quezon City | Water Storage | 324.42 ha
Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife Center | NCR | Quezon City | Pond | 3.39 ha

assignments.limit: The city code crosswalks the printed administrative locality only. It does not establish the identity, location, boundary, extent, access, or current condition of a Jamboree Lake feature.
This administrative locality match does not define reservoir or watershed boundaries, management jurisdiction, fishing access, current fish community, or species presence.

assignments.sourceNameAsPrinted: Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife Center
assignments.limit: Preserve the park label and BMB wetland class as printed. This does not identify a specific pond, establish a waterbody boundary, or support fish presence, access, or public-app inclusion.

limitations: The BMB 2019 inventory is historical and selected; the listed area values are not adopted as current measurements or geometry.
The source does not provide coordinates or feature outlines for these three rows.
The Jamboree Lake and Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife Center entries remain unverified source-row candidates; no canonical waterbody leads are created from a single inventory mention.
The Quezon City and Muntinlupa codes describe administrative localities, not lake or reservoir extents, ownership, access, fishing permission, or legal jurisdiction.
No fish checklist, current presence, safety, regulation, or public-app claim is added; the NCR baseline and Luzon phase remain incomplete.
nextAction: Reconcile these source-row candidates against additional independent NCR waterbody inventories before assigning canonical lead identifiers or boundaries; continue freshwater, brackish, and coastal source review in parallel.
